page: Amazon Web Services i3.xlarge is a storage-optimized instance belonging to the i3 server family. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2686 v4 processor running at 2.3 GHz. The instance features 4 virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. It includes a dedicated CPU allocation with 45 MB of L3 cache, 32 KB of L1d cache, and 0.25 MB of L2 cache. The hardware configuration includes 30.0 GB of system memory, which translates to 7.62 GB of memory per physical core. Storage is a key component of this instance, featuring a bundled 950 GB local NVMe SSD. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps, and the instance operates under the Xen hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates that the i3.xlarge exhibits limited processing and memory performance relative to modern hardware. In CPU-focused tests, the instance recorded a stress-ng single-core performance of 883.17 and a multi-core score of 2080.35, both falling into the bottom 10% of benchmarked servers. Similarly, Geekbench scores reflect this trend, with a single-core score of 898.0 and a multi-core score of 1900.0. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 157.88 GB/sec, but this drops significantly to 22.62 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, and large block write speeds are limited to 14.23 GB/sec. Cryptographic and instruction-set performance, measured via Passmark CPU encryption and extended instructions tests, scored 1700.53 and 2670.97 respectively, placing them in the bottom 25%.

The primary value proposition of the i3.xlarge lies in its local NVMe SSD storage capacity rather than raw computational speed. With 950 GB of high-speed local storage bundled directly with the instance, it offers high resource density for storage-centric tasks, though users must accept the tradeoff of lower CPU and memory performance. This makes the instance qualitatively cost-effective for workloads that require fast local storage access but do not demand high-performance computing. Passmark database operations scored 1513.09, and Redis SET operations reached 2.54 million operations per second. Static web serving throughput is measured at 2.81 GB/sec. Consequently, this instance is best suited for legacy database hosting, caching layers, local storage-heavy logging, and basic web serving where high-speed local storage is prioritized over compute power.
